authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Untrusted network request input
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Attacker-controlled data delivered across a network service boundary.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Attacker-controlled authentication request
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Credentials, factors, or authentication-state inputs supplied to an authentication endpoint.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Attacker-controlled bearer or signed-token input
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A token, token header, or signed-request representation controlled by the requester.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Attacker-controlled URL or hostname
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A URL, redirect destination, origin, or hostname selected by an attacker.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Attacker-controlled protocol peer message
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A message sent by a network protocol participant with attacker-selected state or identity fields.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Cross-site request with ambient victim authentication
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A browser request induced cross-site while carrying the victim's ambient session authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Possession of an existing bearer token
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Prior possession of a valid bearer credential that can be replayed.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Local invocation of an alternate application entrypoint
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A locally available dispatch mechanism used to enter an application through a nonstandard entrypoint.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authentication decision bypass
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: The service establishes or accepts authenticated state without all required authentication evidence succeeding.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unknown-principal acceptance through an empty authentication secret
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An unknown principal is assigned a known empty secret instead of being rejected, making its proof computable.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authenticated-session issuance after failed password verification
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Control flow continues into session issuance after password verification has failed.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authentication acceptance from unresolved asynchronous result truthiness
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An unresolved asynchronous verification object is tested as a Boolean instead of awaiting its resolved result.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authenticated-state promotion through a pre-authentication state-machine error path
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A protocol state machine enters its authenticated state without running successful authentication initialization.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Protected-route access before second-factor completion
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A protected route accepts a session that completed the first factor but not the required second factor.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Application reauthentication bypass through an alternate entrypoint
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An alternate application entrypoint exposes authenticated state without enforcing the application's lock or reauthentication state.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Signed-request authentication with an absent key treated as a known empty secret
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A missing per-principal signing key is interpreted as an empty key, permitting requester-computable signatures.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authorization through an untrusted asserted client identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A requester-controlled identity assertion is accepted as a trusted client identity for access control.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Account-recovery authorization bypass
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An account recovery operation is applied without proof authorizing the affected account.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Victim password reset without a token bound to the affected account
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A reset submission can select another account while omitting a valid reset token for that account.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Credential recovery through an observable or insufficiently bounded verifier
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Authentication verification exposes an oracle or attempt budget that permits systematic credential recovery.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Account-name enumeration through distinguishable authentication failures
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Externally distinguishable failed-login outcomes reveal whether an account name exists.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Second-factor code exhaustion across renewed first-factor sessions
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: The finite second-factor code space can be enumerated because attempt limits do not aggregate across renewed sessions.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Secret-prefix inference through early-exit interactive password comparison
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Prefix-dependent comparison and input behavior exposes observations correlated with a matched secret prefix.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Token verification trust-binding failure
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Untrusted token metadata can change the verification algorithm, key role, or trust root.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: JWT asymmetric-to-symmetric algorithm and key confusion
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An untrusted JWT algorithm selects HMAC verification using public-key bytes intended for asymmetric verification.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: JWT verification under a header-selected JWKS trust root
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Unverified token header fields select the JWKS location and key used to verify that token.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authorization-bearing redirect destination control
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker can select the destination that receives an account-recovery or authentication artifact.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Password-reset link origin poisoning
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Requester-controlled forwarding metadata selects the origin of a token-bearing reset link.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authentication artifact delivery to an attacker-selected redirect audience
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An authentication flow mints and delivers a token to an unauthorized attacker-selected relying-party destination.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Credential destination authority failure
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A credential is suggested, filled, or transmitted to a destination outside its authorized host or origin boundary.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Cross-tenant credential autofill beneath a public suffix
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Credential matching conflates distinct tenants beneath a public suffix and permits user-mediated autofill.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Cross-domain autofill through lossy hostname serialization
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Delimiter-erasing hostname serialization makes structurally distinct domains compare equal.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Cross-origin credential suggestion through single-label suffix matching
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A single-label credential host is treated as a parent suffix of an unrelated dotted hostname.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: API credential forwarding to a substring-matched lookalike host
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A lookalike hostname selects a provider integration and receives its attached API credential.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bearer-token forwarding across an unauthorized redirect host boundary
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A bearer credential for the original host is emitted to a redirected destination without current-host authorization.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authenticated transport identity not bound to in-band participant identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A protocol accepts an embedded participant identity without matching it to the authenticated transport sender.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: DKG participant-slot overwrite through forged sender index
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A peer attributes a node-signature message to another participant and overwrites that participant's state slot.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: FROST DKG share impersonation through unbound message identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A peer submits DKG material labeled as another source share and alters threshold commitments.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Privileged operation reachable without its required authorization context
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A security-sensitive operation is invoked through a weaker or absent authorization context.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: CI configuration evaluation through ambient browser session authority
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: CI linting intended for API-token authority can be invoked with ambient browser-session authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Protected administrative processing after non-terminating authentication redirect
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An unauthenticated redirect does not terminate protected page rendering and administrative processing.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthenticated identity-provisioning account creation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An unauthenticated caller can invoke identity provisioning to create an account.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthenticated recovery-service file operation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A network caller can invoke a recovery sidecar's filesystem-affecting operation without authentication.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Administrative service-task invocation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An authenticated-as-administrator service context permits invocation of privileged internal tasks.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized account credential mutation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker can set or replace another account's authentication credential.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Targeted password guessing against an enumerated account
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A known-valid account identifier enables focused password guessing.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Secret exfiltration through attacker-controlled outbound request construction
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A protected value is interpolated into or attached to a request sent to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Accepted attacker-controlled authorization claims
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A token accepted under attacker-influenced verification supplies authorization-relevant claims.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: File operations under an unauthorized selected identity or path
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker gains read, write, deletion, creation, or truncation operations beyond their authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Privileged operation with skipped authentication initialization
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A privileged command executes after authentication state was forged but required dependent state was never initialized.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bearer-token replay without a temporal validity bound
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A bearer token remains usable indefinitely because it has no expiration bound.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Replay of a disclosed authentication artifact
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A captured authentication artifact can be installed or replayed to act under its represented identity.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Read access to an authorization-protected file
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker can request and receive file content guarded by an authorization check.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Require successful authentication evidence before authenticated state
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Restores the invariant that authenticated state is established only after required evidence succeeds.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Reject unknown principal before secret-proof verification
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Unknown users terminate authentication instead of receiving a default secret.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Terminate authentication after failed password verification
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A failed password result cannot reach session issuance.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Await asynchronous credential verification before the authentication decision
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: The authentication predicate consumes the resolved verification Boolean.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Preserve unauthenticated state until successful authentication initialization
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Error paths cannot promote sessions or expose dependent operations before authentication initialization completes.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Enforce completed second-factor state on every protected route
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Protected routes require server-side state proving completion of the second factor.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Enforce application lock state on every authenticated entrypoint
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: All application entrypoints check reauthentication or lock state before exposing authenticated UI.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Reject signed requests when the principal has no configured secret key
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Absent key material cannot become a known empty signing secret.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bind client authorization to a trusted identity source
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Requester-supplied identity headers cannot independently satisfy client authorization.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Validate and bind account-recovery token to the affected account
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A reset token must be valid and authorize the same account whose credential is changed.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Prevent credential recovery through verifier observations or unbounded attempts
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Restores bounded and externally non-distinguishing credential verification.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Make failed-authentication outcomes externally indistinguishable
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Failure responses do not disclose account existence through observable differences.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Aggregate second-factor attempt bounds across renewed sessions
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Reauthentication cannot reset the attacker's second-factor guessing budget.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Use bounded prefix-independent credential verification
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Credential input and comparison avoid secret-prefix-dependent early exit or interactive timing.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bind token verification to configured algorithms and trust roots
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Untrusted token metadata cannot select an incompatible algorithm, key role, or trust source.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Pin JWT verification to the issuer's asymmetric algorithm and key role
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Only RS256 verification under the configured public key is accepted.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Use a verifier-configured trusted JWKS source
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Verification keys come only from configured issuer trust, not token-supplied URLs.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bind authorization-bearing redirects to approved destinations
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Security artifacts are generated and delivered only for trusted origins or relying parties.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Construct password-reset links from a trusted configured origin
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Requester-controlled forwarding headers cannot choose the reset link destination.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Allow only authorized programmatic authentication redirect destinations
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: JWT audience and delivery destinations are restricted to approved relying parties.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bind credential release to an authorized destination identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Credential suggestion, fill, or transmission occurs only for an authorized host or origin.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Use public-suffix-aware exact-host credential matching
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Credentials for public-suffix tenants are suggested only on the exact tenant hostname.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Preserve hostname structure in credential-domain comparison
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Domain serialization or comparison cannot erase label boundaries.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Require full-origin equality for single-label credential hosts
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Single-label and root-level hosts cannot authorize unrelated dotted hostnames by suffix.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Require exact approved-host membership before attaching provider credentials
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Lookalike or substring-matched hosts are rejected before credential-bearing requests.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authorize the current destination host before bearer emission
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A bearer header is emitted only if credentials are allowed for the current redirect destination.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bind in-band participant identity to authenticated transport identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Messages are accepted only when claimed sender and recipient identities match authenticated peers and valid ranges.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Require the intended authorization context before privileged operation execution
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Sensitive operations reject weaker, absent, or incomplete authorization contexts.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Require API-token authentication before CI configuration evaluation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Cookie-only browser sessions cannot reach CI lint evaluation.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authenticate requests at the identity-provisioning route boundary
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Unauthenticated requests cannot reach SCIM resource operations.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Deploy fixed endpoint authentication or disable the exposed service
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A sensitive sidecar operation is protected by a fixed implementation or removed from exposure.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Upgrade to a fixed implementation with undisclosed corrective mechanism
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Used only where evidence identifies a fixed release but not the exact implementation change.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Bound bearer-token lifetime and reject expired tokens
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Issued bearer tokens include an expiration and are rejected after it.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized access
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Access to a protected account, service, or operation without the required authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized administrative service access
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Unauthorized access to a service with administrative authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Account takeover
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: The attacker obtains authenticated control of another user's account.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized account access without the required second factor
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An account is accessed with only the first factor despite a second-factor requirement.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Authentication boundary bypass
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A requester is treated as authenticated without valid required credentials.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized protected-route or application access
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A protected route or authenticated application area is exposed without its required access condition.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Confidentiality disclosure
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Protected information is disclosed to an unauthorized party.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Credential or authentication-artifact disclosure
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Passwords, API keys, bearer tokens, or authentication artifacts are disclosed.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Protected application-data disclosure
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Application secrets, flags, files, or protected variables are disclosed.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Cryptographic secret-key recovery
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A distributed or threshold cryptographic secret key is reconstructed by an unauthorized participant.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Integrity loss
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Protected state, credentials, identities, or files are modified without authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized file creation, modification, deletion, or truncation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Filesystem content or existence is changed without authority.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized identity or account creation
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker creates or changes identity-provider account state without authorization.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Availability loss
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: A service or protocol cannot continue providing its intended function.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Service process crash
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An invalid execution path terminates the service process.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Distributed key-generation ceremony disruption
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Manipulated participant state prevents or disrupts DKG completion.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Server-side code execution
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: Attacker-controlled code executes in a server or service process context.

authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.concept: Unauthorized actions under a replayed identity
authentication_and_credentials::part-01:.description: An attacker performs otherwise authorized operations using a replayed victim or server identity.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::src..description: An external actor controls request, message, path, identifier, header, parameter, or callback data crossing into a service or contract.
A caller has a valid identity or limited role but controls an operation selector or resource reference beyond intended authority.
An attacker possesses, induces, or benefits from a credential, approval, endorsement, or workload identity with delegated authority.
A trusted workflow, bot, callback, import, policy, or bootstrap process consumes attacker-influenced state.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::src..concept: code execution in a constrained isolate
authorization_and_tenants::part-01::src..description: Attacker code already executes inside a sandboxed or otherwise constrained process.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::cap..description: Authority is evaluated against a principal, tenant, object, method, thread, or workflow context different from the operation's actual target.
A caller selects or resolves a resource outside the caller's authorized object set.
A nonprivileged caller invokes or commits an administrator, governance, policy, or other privileged operation.
Delegated authority is exercised for a different owner, caller, module, operator, or callback than the authority was intended to cover.
An authenticated identity is rebound to an attacker-selected tenant, organization, database, or namespace.
A workflow, pipeline, token, or process executes under an attacker-selected or spoofable principal.
Validation or authorization and later interpretation operate on different representations of the same security-sensitive input or target.
Different stages derive different security identities or structured values from the same attacker-controlled representation.
Authorization classifies one path representation while later routing or rewriting reaches another target.
Client-controlled data becomes trusted role, identity, recursion, or authorization state.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::cap..concept: client-controlled role or identity claim acceptance
authorization_and_tenants::part-01::cap..description: A client-selected role or identity value is signed, parsed, or trusted as authoritative.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::cap..concept: client injection of internal control metadata
authorization_and_tenants::part-01::cap..description: Externally supplied metadata is accepted as framework-internal control state.
An attacker-selected operation or target is executed with ambient service, server, system, or configured-tool authority.
A semantically equivalent input, participant, operation, or entrypoint is omitted from an otherwise intended policy.
A caller selects a value outside an allowlist, maximum, restriction list, or confinement policy.
A user-code or command-bearing execution surface omits the authorization or allowlist applied to equivalent surfaces.
Ordering, lifecycle, snapshot, or workflow state lets an actor cross a guard enforced only in another state or step.
A representation produced under one credential context is replayed to a different context.
An actor crosses a sandbox, desktop integrity, cluster-member, or workload confinement boundary.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::mit..description: Resolve or return a selected object only within the requester-authorized owner, customer, group, tenant, or organization scope.
Authorize every entrypoint and workflow step that can commit a privileged operation.
Bind delegated, callback, pipeline, token, or module authority to the intended authenticated principal or designated component.
Validate and authorize the same canonical identity, path, target, or decoded structure later consumed.
Derive role and internal control state from authenticated server-controlled provenance, rejecting client-forged state.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::mit..concept: complete policy enforcement across equivalent surfaces
authorization_and_tenants::part-01::mit..description: Apply allowlists, limits, restrictions, and authorization checks to every semantically equivalent input and execution surface.
Prevent attacker-selected targets from inheriting ambient credentials or configured server authority.
Preserve authorization and snapshot invariants across lifecycle, ordering, and multi-step workflow transitions.
Do not publicly reuse representations derived from authenticated requests across credential contexts.
Restore process, desktop, workload, or member-cluster isolation through scoped identities and inaccessible peer authority.
Use a vendor-fixed implementation when available artifacts do not establish the corrective mechanism.

authorization_and_tenants::part-01::imp..description: Unauthorized disclosure of PII, account, order, ticket, profile, or event data.
Unauthorized disclosure of passwords, signing keys, API keys, tokens, secrets, or secret-bearing content.
Unauthorized disclosure of documents, repository content, messages, metrics, or application-rendered content.
Access to an account, resource, application, tenant, or operation without required authority.
Acquisition of administrator, staff, root, or equivalent privileged authority.
Execution of a protected administrative, governance, deletion, sharing, or management operation.
Unauthorized modification, poisoning, deletion, or manipulation of protected state.
Unauthorized movement or removal of tokens or other assets.
Loss or degradation of service, account, or resource availability.
Execution of attacker-controlled commands or code under a service or privileged process identity.
Escape from a sandbox, desktop integrity boundary, workload confinement, or member-cluster boundary.
A configured authorization, confinement, approval, or placement policy is defeated without a separately evidenced downstream asset effect.

cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.description: An adversary selects ciphertexts, public values, points, signatures, or protocol parameters consumed by a cryptographic operation.
An adversary obtains repeated operation timings together with related public cryptographic outputs.
An active network-path adversary can modify, suppress, or substitute protocol traffic.
A cryptographic parser or verifier receives an attacker-selected noncanonical, invalid, or boundary-case encoding.
An adversary supplies keys, signatures, certificates, assertions, tokens, or identity claims used in an authorization decision.
A key, nonce, prime, setup secret, or token secret is generated with predictable or structurally weak material.
A replay, reorganization, lifecycle change, or authorized state update drives a security-sensitive state machine.
An adversary supplies structured bytes, metadata, coordinates, vectors, or fields consumed by a parser or computation.
A storage-controlling adversary can supply or modify persistent volume content or metadata.
A former authorized recipient retains cryptographic material after authorization is revoked.
Secret-dependent execution produces an attacker-observable timing, cache, error, or diagnostic distinction.
Pointer-like secret-influenced data causes a hardware prefetch whose cache effect is observed by a co-resident attacker.
Signing duration reveals noisy information about the bit length or leading-zero structure of an ECDSA nonce.
Division on a secret-derived numerator creates an externally distinguishable timing signal.
Malformed ciphertext processing exposes a distinguishable padding-validity or padding-error signal.
Data-dependent comparison of an attacker-supplied authentication tag reveals prefix-match timing information.
DH shared-secret representation or KDF processing reveals whether the secret begins with zero bytes.
Diagnostic output reveals branch-dependent events from a secret-key computation.
Partial observations or structural weaknesses are combined to reconstruct a long-term cryptographic secret.

cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.concept: Lattice reconstruction from partial secret constraints
cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.description: Partial nonce, coefficient, or prime constraints are solved with lattice or related small-root techniques to recover a key.
Publicly detectable prime-generation structure enables specialized factorization and private-key reconstruction.
A downgraded or weak finite-field DH group permits discrete-log recovery of traffic secrets.
A trusted identity or key is interpreted under attacker-substituted cryptographic parameters.
A peer can select a signature algorithm or hash that policy should reject as obsolete.

cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.concept: Cryptographic scalar or key-domain admission bypass
cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.description: A verifier or key API admits a scalar, key, point, or runtime value outside its required domain.
Missing nonzero scalar checks cause an all-zero ECDSA signature to verify.
A signature verifier accepts a scalar representative outside the canonical group-order range.

cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.concept: Runtime type coercion to predictable private scalar
cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.description: An invalid runtime value is coerced to a predictable private-key scalar instead of being rejected.
An externally supplied point is admitted without required curve, subgroup, identity, or encoding checks.

cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.concept: Neutral group element propagation through protocol arithmetic
cryptographic_and_certificate_validation.description: An accepted identity element remains neutral through scalar multiplication and degenerates later protocol processing.
A decoder accepts an encoding that the protocol requires to be rejected.
An out-of-modulus field representation reaches a fallible conversion whose error is panicked or propagated into liveness failure.
Different parsers or representations resolve the same bytes to different security-relevant objects.
The content consumed for identity or authorization is not the exact content selected and authenticated by the signature reference.
A TLS connection is encrypted but the peer certificate or server name is not authenticated.
A certificate chain is accepted on a path that fails to apply required revocation checking.
Malformed or omitted IP name data avoids the issuer's permitted or excluded name constraints.
An update verifier omits required certificate-chain validation and accepts attacker-selected signing authority.
A protocol accepts an identity without the required proof of credential possession or signature validity.
An untrusted aggregate co-signer key participates in authorization without proof of possession.
Peer-supplied negotiation state disables a server-required certificate proof check.
A client certificate listed in a CRL remains accepted on one authentication path.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.e.description: Untrusted input controls XML construction and external entity resource resolution.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.c.description: Memory corruption is developed into control over native process or kernel dispatch.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.f.concept: Virtual dispatch through attacker-arranged object metadata
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.f.description: Corrupted object state redirects a virtual call through attacker-arranged dispatch metadata.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.r.description: Return-address control is developed into a ROP chain that executes process operations or commands.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.h.description: Corrupted metadata redirects an allocator hook, callback, or dispatch target.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.a.concept: Trusted authentication state acquisition or manipulation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.a.description: An exploit obtains or writes trusted authentication material used by a verifier.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.r.concept: Resource or work-item accounting invariant violation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.r.description: A count used to bound work omits or underflows outstanding elements.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::cap.a.description: Malformed input reaches a panic, fault, or allocator rejection that terminates processing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.b.concept: Enforce concrete storage bounds before access
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.b.description: Validate index, count, length, cursor, or segment extent against the actual destination or source storage.
Limit copy or concatenation to remaining destination capacity.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.s.description: Check lower and upper bounds before using a signed value as an index or offset.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.p.description: Use the actual resource allocation or segment metadata rather than generic maxima.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.p.concept: Bound parser-derived counts to destination capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.p.description: Propagate capacity and reject token or sequence counts that cannot fit.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.c.concept: Enforce conversion success, encoding, and output-capacity contracts
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.c.description: Reject conversion failures or invalid encodings before offset arithmetic and ensure output capacity.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.c.concept: Canonicalize or reject noncanonical encoded values
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.c.description: Require canonical byte alignment or encoding before pairwise or fixed-offset decoding.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.l.concept: Retain object lifetime across unlocked or deferred use
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.l.description: Hold locks, references, or mapping-owned backing state until all uses complete.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.s.description: Prevent transitions whose required cloning, ownership, or cleanup semantics are unavailable.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.o.description: Make ownership transfer, destruction, and release paths consistent with storage provenance, including unwind paths.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.p.concept: Preserve parser identity, ordering, and extent state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.p.description: Carry required source-order, identity, or parser-state facts across reparsing and processing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.n.concept: Restrict attacker reachability to the vulnerable service
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.n.description: Remove or heavily constrain external access pending a mechanism-level fix.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.f.description: Use a vendor-fixed release when artifacts do not establish the exact invariant-restoring code change.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.a.concept: Correct complete resource and work-item accounting
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.a.description: Include all outstanding elements and decrement remaining work under explicit bounds.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.o.concept: Respect opaque object and application ownership boundaries
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::mit.o.description: Do not dereference undocumented object internals; use application-owned buffers and metadata.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.c.description: Unauthorized disclosure of protected data or memory.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.p.description: Unauthorized disclosure of bytes from process memory.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.f.description: Unauthorized disclosure of files readable by the affected process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.i.description: Unauthorized corruption of data, object state, or memory without an established stronger boundary consequence.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.m.description: Out-of-bounds access, use-after-free, double free, or related memory corruption.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.v.description: A decoder returns a binary value different from the represented input.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.a.description: Attacker-triggered loss of service or processing availability.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.p.description: A user-space process panics, aborts, or crashes.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.k.concept: Kernel, backend, or host denial of service
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.k.description: A kernel, hypervisor backend, or host faults or terminates.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.c.concept: Unauthorized native code or command execution
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.c.description: Attacker obtains unauthorized execution in a native process or kernel context.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.p.description: Unauthorized execution in a server, client, appliance, browser subprocess, or desktop-user process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.k.concept: Kernel-context code execution or privilege escalation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.k.description: Unauthorized kernel execution or equivalent local elevation to kernel/root authority.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.a.description: Trusted authentication state is satisfied or bypassed without the required secret.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.i.description: Compromise crosses a guest, sandbox, renderer, or other isolation boundary.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-01::imp.h.description: A guest compromises the host-side virtualization process.
A stale host mapping may permit confidentiality, integrity, or availability compromise across the guest boundary.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::src_r.description: A remote peer controls protocol, request, image, module, or script data consumed by a service or process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::src_l.description: A local process or library caller controls arguments, files, socket operations, or standard input reaching the affected component.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::src_g.description: A guest or sandboxed process controls requests or shared fields consumed across a host, kernel, hypervisor, or sandbox boundary.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::src_i.concept: Lower-privilege control of shared privileged state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::src_i.description: A lower-privilege component can modify shared state later trusted by a more privileged component.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_i.description: Processing consumes a field or state without establishing the presence, shape, or metadata contract required by the consumer.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_m.concept: Missing-value buffer access and response overread
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_m.description: Key presence is mistaken for value existence, causing stale or invalid value-associated memory to be read and returned.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_u.description: Object or parser state is consumed before construction establishes a defined initial value.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_c.description: A callback or virtual operation receives an argument that violates the callee's required validity contract.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_t.description: Untrusted metadata is propagated into a fixed-layout typed object instead of being derived from the concrete type.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.description: A dispatch classifier selects a handler whose operation class or calling signature is incompatible with supplied arguments.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_t.concept: Unchecked type-table index and indirect dispatch
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_t.description: An unvalidated serialized type identifier indexes a method table and selects an indirect call target.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_r.description: Storage containing one runtime object type is consumed through an incompatible object interface.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_r.concept: Reentrant lookup coherence failure leading to type confusion
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_r.description: A callback mutates receiver state during lookup, after which stale lookup assumptions create incompatible descriptor and value typing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_m.description: An address, index, range, output cursor, or mapping extent escapes the storage or aperture it is required to remain within.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_u.concept: Unchecked indexed memory read and write
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_u.description: A caller-controlled index is used for element access without enforcing the stored collection bound.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_f.description: Duplicate or expansion semantics produce more output entries than a fixed destination can hold.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.concept: Decoder or decoding-table output exceeds allocation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.description: Attacker-controlled encoded data causes decoder output or table construction to write beyond its allocated destination.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: A parser-produced range is applied to its backing buffer without proving that the range remains within the buffer.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.concept: Oversized protocol length reaches bounded handler
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: A decoded protocol length exceeding the handler's supported maximum reaches downstream processing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_o.concept: Exclusive-upper-bound equality accepted for table access
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_o.description: An index equal to an exclusive upper bound is admitted and selects the first out-of-range fixed-stride table entry.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_b.concept: Scaled bitmap operation modifies adjacent state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_b.description: An attacker-influenced bitmap position or range is scaled incorrectly and performs a relative bit operation outside the bitmap.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_m.description: A user-selected mapping length extends a device MMIO mapping beyond its physical aperture into unrelated physical memory.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_u.concept: Unbounded field input overwrites adjacent state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_u.description: A string or delimited field is written into fixed storage without a destination-capacity bound, corrupting adjacent data or control state.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_m.description: An object is accessed, referenced, or released inconsistently with its ownership and lifetime state.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.concept: Duplicate release through competing ownership aliases
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.description: Multiple aliases or cleanup paths independently release one allocation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_e.concept: Post-return use of escaped stack storage
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_e.description: A pointer to callee stack storage remains usable after the frame allocation is reclaimed.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.concept: Use after free through retained owner pointer
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_d.description: Cleanup frees a nested object but leaves an owning field pointing to the released storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_q.description: Queue and side-reference state diverge so an object freed by one receive path remains selectable by another.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_l.description: A delayed or concurrent path increments a reference through a stale pointer without proving that the object remains live.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_r.concept: Premature reference release across destructive unlink
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_r.description: A temporary reference is dropped before unlink consumes the queue reference, allowing later reference acquisition on freed storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_e.description: An API permits multiple live mutable references to the same object or attachment.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: Formatting a pointer value incorrectly requires pointee validity and dereferences an invalid pointer.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_s.description: A race exposes a resource in combinations of ownership, allocation, and reference state forbidden by its lifecycle invariants.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: Concurrent page transfer exposes allocated, owner, and reference-count states in inconsistent combinations.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_s.concept: Untrusted shared offset selects privileged memory copy
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_s.description: An application-writable shared offset is used directly to construct privileged memory copy addresses.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_c.description: A privileged component dereferences an address selected through writable lower-privilege shared state.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_c.concept: Attacker-directed memory read or write primitive
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_c.description: The attacker can direct bounded or arbitrary reads or writes to selected addresses.
Memory corruption or a directed write changes native control flow to an attacker-selected computation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.concept: Command or native code execution in target process
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: The capability executes attacker-selected native code or operating-system commands in the affected process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.concept: Privileged-context memory read or write primitive
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_p.description: The attacker obtains selected memory access in a kernel, hypervisor, trusted application, or privileged master.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::cap_a.description: Input intended for a noncredential field overwrites credential data consumed by an authentication decision.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.concept: Enforce required input state before consumption
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.description: Reject or safely handle input whose required value, state, or callback argument is absent or invalid.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_i.description: Construction establishes defined sentinel or initial values before later state handling.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.concept: Enforce storage, index, range, or aperture bounds
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.description: Validate access extent against the concrete destination, collection, buffer, table, or device aperture before use.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_b.concept: Bind parsing and input writes to destination capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_b.description: Use destination-sized parsing or copying and reject components that do not fit.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_v.concept: Derive or validate structural metadata before use
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_v.description: Use type-derived constants or validate serialized type, length, and layout metadata before dispatch or copying.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.description: Coordinate ownership, references, cleanup, and pointer invalidation so objects remain live while used and are released once.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_s.concept: Scope exclusive access to prevent retained aliases
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_s.description: Redesign traversal so mutable access cannot remain live across another path to the same object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_a.concept: Make resource lifecycle transition atomic and coherent
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_a.description: Pin and transition allocation, reference, ownership, and list state without exposing forbidden intermediate combinations.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.description: Restart or complete lookup after callbacks so mutations made during reentrancy are observed before storing or dispatching.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.concept: Prevent untrusted state from selecting privileged addresses
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_r.description: Use trusted derived addresses, inline bounded storage, or authorization checks rather than untrusted offsets or pointers.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::mit_u.description: Apply the reported fixed release when artifacts do not reveal the precise corrective mechanism.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_c.description: Protected information becomes observable to an unauthorized actor.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_p.description: Bytes from process memory are returned or exposed remotely.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_k.description: Kernel, hypervisor, trusted-application, or privileged process memory is disclosed.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_a.description: A process, service, appliance, or kernel becomes unavailable.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_p.description: The affected process or isolated service terminates or aborts.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_k.description: A kernel or hypervisor panic, fault, or memory leak causes denial of service.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_m.description: Undefined behavior or sanitizer-detected invalid memory access is established without a stronger demonstrated outcome.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_c.description: Attacker-selected native code or commands execute in the affected security context.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_p.concept: Code execution in application or service process
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_p.description: Attacker-selected code or commands execute in a non-browser target process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_b.concept: Browser renderer or browser-process code execution
parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_b.description: Attacker-controlled native execution occurs in a browser process or renderer context.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_p.description: The attacker crosses a local privilege boundary to a more privileged user or kernel context.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_i.description: A guest, sandbox, or compartment compromises the integrity of a more privileged isolation domain.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-02::imp_a.description: An authentication decision is satisfied without possession of the required credential.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::src_u.description: Attacker-controlled structured data reaches a parser, decoder, document reader, protocol handler, or serializer.
Attacker-controlled bytecode, JavaScript, WebAssembly, eBPF, or VM instructions are compiled, verified, interpreted, or executed.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::src_l.concept: Attacker-controlled local API and lifecycle operations
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::src_l.description: Local API, ioctl, file-descriptor, object-lifetime, teardown, or concurrency operations under attacker influence.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::src_c.description: Messages cross a process isolation boundary into a privileged or separately sandboxed receiver.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_s.description: An access escapes the valid bounds of its intended object, array, buffer, or guest-memory region.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_o.description: Attacker-influenced indexing, length, or pointer arithmetic writes beyond an authorized destination range.
Attacker-influenced indexing, length, or pointer arithmetic reads beyond an authorized source range.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_u.description: An unvalidated opcode or program counter selects an out-of-domain indirect call target.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_t.description: A pointer or reference remains usable after the referenced storage lifetime has ended.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_e.description: A returned object retains a reference into callee stack storage that is dead after return.
A long-lived object or foreign library retains caller-owned bytes beyond their guaranteed lifetime.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.concept: Callback-driven object invalidation with resumed stale use
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.description: Reentrant callback activity destroys an object that resumed processing later dereferences.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_t.concept: Cross-subsystem teardown leaves a stale external reference
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_t.description: Teardown frees backing storage while another subsystem or open interface retains a dereferenceable reference.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.description: One operation frees an object while a concurrent operation retains and uses it without sufficient locking or lifetime retention.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_a.concept: Unsound compiler or verifier abstract state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_a.description: A compiler or verifier model excludes concrete runtime values, provenance, registers, stack state, or control-flow outcomes later trusted for safety.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_j.description: Optimized numeric type or range facts fail to conservatively represent a concrete runtime value used for memory access.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.description: Compiler bookkeeping records register, spill, or instance state not established on every runtime path.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_v.description: A verifier restores pointer authority to a transformed scalar without proving original bounded provenance.
A verifier transfer function fails to over-approximate concrete scalar results later used as pointer offsets.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_r.description: Logic for one object representation is applied after a state transition produces an incompatible representation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_p.description: Parser or decoder state is consumed despite an invalid status, incomplete structure, inconsistent cursor, or incompatible layout contract.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_s.description: An error status and a positional or length value share a representation, allowing failed processing to continue with an invalid boundary.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_e.description: Encoding conversion and input reset ordering leave parser cursors inconsistent with buffered data.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_f.description: Code performs a fixed-offset slice or field extraction without first establishing the required input type and length.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_i.concept: Incomplete fixed-width header causes parser non-progress
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_i.description: A parser consumes or retries an incomplete fixed-width header without a boundary guard, causing non-termination.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_r.concept: Unsafe synchronous reentrancy across a fragile lifecycle boundary
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_r.description: Synchronous script or callback execution mutates or destroys state while a non-reentrant lifecycle phase still relies on it.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_a.description: Security authority is retained, restored, or derived from state that does not prove the current actor or object's entitlement.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_p.description: A descriptor retains privilege conferred by an earlier caller and authorizes later operations without rechecking the current caller.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_f.concept: Diagnostic fault context used as continuation authority
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_f.description: Attacker-reachable crash-stack or diagnostic bytes are treated as authoritative saved-context continuation inputs.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_m.concept: Arbitrary or broad memory read/write primitive
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_m.description: A preceding memory-safety or verifier flaw is developed into attacker-directed memory reads and writes.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.description: Attacker-controlled state redirects a code entry, return, callback, function pointer, handler, or indirect call.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_p.concept: Unauthorized reachability of a privileged evaluator
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_p.description: Memory confusion or authority failure reaches an evaluator reserved for an authorized principal.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_r.concept: Response length exceeds initialized buffer extent
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_r.description: A transmitted length reflects would-have-written output rather than initialized buffer bytes, disclosing adjacent memory.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_i.description: Modular arithmetic makes an out-of-range offset-plus-length request appear to satisfy a bounds check.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_s.description: Pointer traversal applies a scalar-unit stride to a wider typed pointer and escapes the intended allocation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_g.description: Guest-controlled stack or memory addressing dereferences host memory outside the allocated guest region.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.concept: Memory corruption in a cross-process IPC receiver
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_c.description: Attacker-controlled IPC corrupts memory in a separately sandboxed or privileged receiving process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::cap_n.description: Malformed input causes a parser or decoder to loop without progress.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_b.concept: Enforce object and range bounds before access
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_b.description: Restore spatial safety by validating indexes, offsets, lengths, pointer ranges, and destination capacities before memory access.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_o.description: Validate representability and containment without relying on a potentially wrapping offset-plus-length sum.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_l.concept: Restore object lifetime and ownership validity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_l.description: Ensure referenced storage remains live or references are invalidated and drained before destruction.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_t.concept: Drain external references before backing-object teardown
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_t.description: Deregister, synchronize, or drain cross-subsystem users before freeing backing storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_c.concept: Synchronize concurrent object use and reclamation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_c.description: Use locking, references, or grace periods so active users cannot race object deletion.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_a.concept: Preserve sound compiler or verifier state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_a.description: Require abstract state to conservatively model all concrete values, provenance, and control-flow outcomes before safety decisions.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_p.description: Restore parser contracts by separating status from values, validating structure availability, and preserving coherent cursor state.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_r.concept: Prevent synchronous mutation during fragile lifecycle work
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_r.description: Forbid, defer, or safely accommodate callbacks that could destroy state during non-reentrant processing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_c.concept: Bind authority to the current actor and valid provenance
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_c.description: Revalidate present authority and reject latent or reconstructed authority not tied to current proof.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_i.concept: Keep diagnostic metadata non-authoritative for continuation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_i.description: Do not derive execution continuation or saved-context arguments from compromised diagnostic or interrupted-stack data.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_u.description: Use a vendor-fixed release when the available artifacts do not establish the implementation-level repair.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_r.description: Eliminate an API that exposes internal kernel object ownership or pointer semantics to untrusted callers.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_r.concept: Bound transmitted length to initialized output capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_r.description: Transmit formatted output only when its reported length is within the initialized destination buffer.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::mit_m.description: Validate and safely decode renderer-originated IPC without overflowing receiver buffers.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_c.description: Attacker-selected instructions, commands, script, or native code execute in the affected process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_p.description: Native instructions or operating-system commands execute in the affected user-space process.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_r.description: Native code execution occurs in a browser renderer process or its renderer sandbox.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_p.description: An attacker gains execution or authority at a more privileged operating-system boundary.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_k.description: Attacker control reaches kernel authority, root credentials, or equivalent device-level privilege.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_c.description: Information outside the attacker's authorized view is disclosed.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_s.description: A protected file, flag, or challenge secret becomes readable.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_a.description: Processing or service availability is lost through crash, panic, abort, or non-termination.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_k.description: A kernel fault or panic disrupts system availability.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-03::imp_n.description: A parser or decoder loops indefinitely and fails to complete processing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_u.description: A remote peer controls protocol data consumed by a service.

A local or embedded caller controls API objects, lengths, offsets, or operation ordering.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_s.description: Script controls browser-engine operations and object state.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_c.description: Concurrent teardown, collection, cancellation, or reference acquisition is attacker-influenced.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_p.description: A caller with the required kernel capability submits a verifier-checked program.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_g.description: A guest controls MMIO or DMA-like device operation parameters.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::src_i.description: An IPC client supplies an identifier used to select a privileged-service object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_l.description: An operation can retain, reclaim, or use an object inconsistently with its ownership lifetime.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_r.description: Reference or handle accounting understates live users and allows early reclamation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.description: One owner retains objects belonging to independently reclaimed storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_u.description: An object is handed to another subsystem or worker without retaining its lifetime through use.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_g.description: An external reference can be acquired without serialization against specialized object GC.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.concept: Unrestored evaluator context exposes stale state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.description: Nested evaluation fails to restore context state, allowing later use after the referenced state becomes invalid.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_o.description: Attacker-influenced state permits a read or write outside an allocated object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_i.concept: Index or cursor exceeds destination capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_i.description: An index, cursor, or element count is not constrained to the destination allocation before writing.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_a.concept: Aggregate output expansion exceeds buffer capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_a.description: Combined or rendered output length is not bounded against remaining storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_s.description: Offset, length, overflow, and backing-size constraints are not jointly enforced.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_p.concept: Allocation pointer and capacity metadata desynchronization
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_p.description: Failed resizing leaves an old allocation paired with inflated capacity metadata.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_f.concept: Fixed-length transfer starts inside a same-sized buffer
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_f.description: A fixed-size transfer uses a nonzero in-buffer offset without reducing or validating transfer length.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_p.description: Accepted input drives parser state outside the invariants required by later operations.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.concept: Parser state transition bypasses mandatory semantic validation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.description: A conditional parser transition skips validation required for a safely constructed object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_p.concept: Unmatched grammar transition underflows parser stack
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_p.description: An unmatched close transition decrements a local parser stack below its base.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.description: Interpreter-visible traversal follows links intended only for implementation bookkeeping.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_u.concept: Unsound abstract-state pruning accepts unsafe continuation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_u.description: Verifier state equivalence omits precision facts needed to prove later pointer operations safe.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_t.description: An identifier-selected object is used as a required subtype without runtime subtype validation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_j.concept: JIT side-effect model preserves pointer across hidden mutation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_j.description: An operation modeled as load-only can mutate and reallocate storage while generated code retains its old address.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_a.concept: Heap allocator metadata control from repeated stale frees
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_a.description: Repeated deallocation and overlap permit corruption of allocator freelist links.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_c.description: A write or forged dispatch target redirects native execution to an attacker-selected function or chain.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_k.concept: Arbitrary kernel memory read and write
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::cap_k.description: An attacker can read and modify attacker-selected kernel memory.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_l.concept: Restore object lifetime and ownership consistency
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_l.description: Ensure aliases, owners, references, and asynchronous users cannot outlive reclaimed storage.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_a.concept: Invalidate all aliases and ownership entries before deallocation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_a.description: Remove every reachable alias or ownership entry before freeing an object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.concept: Remove public construction of unsound ownership handles
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.description: Prevent callers from obtaining handles whose lifetime protocol cannot be upheld.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.concept: Pin referenced objects through asynchronous use
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.description: Acquire and hold a reference under the required lock until the consumer has acquired ownership.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_l.concept: Serialize cancellation, collection, and reference transitions
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_l.description: Order lifecycle transitions so collection or cancellation cannot disagree with an active user.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_c.concept: Save and restore nested evaluator context state
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_c.description: Restore the evaluator's context object after nested evaluation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_b.concept: Enforce allocation-derived memory bounds before access
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_b.description: Reject operations whose complete access range does not fit the destination allocation.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_i.concept: Guard index, cursor, or count against destination capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_i.description: Use allocation- or layout-derived capacity before indexed writes.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_a.concept: Validate aggregate expanded length against remaining capacity
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_a.description: Account for all components and formatting expansion before concatenation or rendering.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.concept: Validate offset-length slices with overflow-safe arithmetic
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.description: Reject null, negative, overflowed, or backing-array-exceeding slices.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_t.concept: Commit resized pointer and capacity only after allocation succeeds
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_t.description: Keep old pointer and capacity paired until a replacement allocation succeeds.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.concept: Restore parser and state-machine transition invariants
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.description: Reject state transitions that cannot produce a semantically valid downstream object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.concept: Remove obsolete parsing transition that bypasses validation
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_r.description: Delete a legacy parse branch whose state transition skips mandatory checks.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_b.concept: Enforce same-lifecycle grammar balance and stack bounds
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_b.description: Require matching transitions and validate stack bounds before pointer movement.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.concept: Separate implementation metadata from interpreter-visible topology
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.description: Represent bookkeeping links outside fields traversed by the interpreter.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_v.concept: Preserve precision facts during verifier state pruning
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_v.description: Retain abstract-state precision required to reject unsafe pointer continuations.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.concept: Validate resolved object subtype before specialized dispatch
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_s.description: Reject an object unless its runtime subtype matches the handler's required type.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_d.concept: Remove or disable optimization with unsound side-effect model
parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::mit_d.description: Avoid optimized code generation where hidden mutation invalidates retained pointers.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::imp_m.description: Memory outside the intended object is corrupted or used after its lifetime.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::imp_s.description: A stack-resident object is overwritten beyond its bounds.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::imp_k.description: Kernel-resident memory is modified outside the intended object.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::imp_k.description: The operating-system kernel terminates or panics.

parser_and_memory_safety::part-04::imp_f.description: A challenge flag or equivalent packaged secret is disclosed.
