protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::s.description: Untrusted data or protocol actions supplied remotely to a network service.
Local operations through syscalls, IPC, filesystems, networking configuration, or device lifecycle interfaces.
A transaction or privileged configuration action which changes smart-contract protocol state.
Web content or JavaScript executing within a browser-facing boundary.
An adversary able to intercept and modify an in-flight protocol byte stream.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Security-relevant state lifecycle violation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to drive state through an invalid transition or retain state beyond its valid lifecycle.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Constituent and reassembled message dual dispatch
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to dispatch both fragments and their reconstructed message as independent requests, violating single-message lifecycle integrity.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Pre-authentication identity state exposure
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to make authorization-visible identity state reflect an asserted principal before credential verification commits.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Custody-routing configuration inconsistency
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to create a configuration in which custody remains in one component while settlement routing no longer accesses it.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Irreversible settlement before successful value delivery
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to commit final settlement state despite a failed, non-retryable value transfer.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Assertion on a fallible operation result
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to route an expected operation error into a fatal assertion rather than normal error handling.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Security-decision representation confusion
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to obtain a different security decision from semantically related but non-identical representations.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Noncanonical numeric representation authorization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to pass an authorization gate using alternate text that parses to an accepted numeric value.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Authorization-routing path representation divergence
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to make authorization inspect a path different from the path used for route execution.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Asynchronous object-lifetime violation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for deferred or asynchronous work to access state after its valid lifetime ends.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Completion callback access after teardown
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for an outstanding asynchronous completion callback to access an object freed during teardown.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Shared dependency unavailability by state-dependent rejection
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to make a common read or dependency path reject and thereby block multiple dependent operations.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Synchronous re-entry into a held non-reentrant lock
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to re-enter an operation and reacquire the same non-reentrant lock on one execution path.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Permissionless refresh of a privileged-operation cooldown
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for an untrusted caller to reset shared freshness state so a required privileged transition reverts.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Invalid configuration admitted to a runtime path
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to install a semantically incompatible configuration which later reaches code assuming the excluded invariant.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Circuit-breaker-disputed value persisted as fallback state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for a value rejected by cross-source integrity checks to replace a trusted fallback anchor.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Browser JavaScript execution in a privileged browsing context
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in a browser context holding elevated origin or user state.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Downstream HTTP message-boundary manipulation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for attacker-influenced field data to become structural HTTP framing during proxy serialization.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Script-readable privileged response exfiltration
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to turn a privileged backend response into script-readable data and transmit it externally.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Stale browser action accepted after navigation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to apply a queued user-interface action created for an old document to a newly current document context.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: JavaScript execution in another origin context
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to execute attacker-controlled browser JavaScript with a different origin's opener or document authority.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Authorization enforced after an irreversible side effect
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to reach a billable or security-sensitive phase before the relevant authorization decision is applied.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Reentrant mutation of an assumed-stable state machine
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for an attacker-controlled callback to mutate lifecycle state during an operation that assumes stability.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Operation invoked on an incompatible object lifecycle state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to invoke an operation whose initialization or lifecycle preconditions are false for the target object state.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Connection shutdown nontermination
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to keep a connection waiting indefinitely after a fatal event precludes its expected clean-shutdown completion.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Page-controlled interruption of security-warning navigation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for hostile page script to stop a warning redirect used as the enforcement boundary.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Protocol-specific authorization reached through an incompatible endpoint
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to invoke an authorization implementation through an endpoint that bypasses its assumed protocol state.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Certificate signing without required protocol authorization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to obtain certificate signing after bypassing the provisioner's intended authorization flow.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Pending authority transition survives emergency recovery
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for a queued authority change to remain executable after emergency replacement of compromised authority.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Post-recovery recapture of privileged authority
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to restore attacker-controlled authority after an emergency recovery transition.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Reuse of expired bootstrap authorization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to use a one-time setup credential after bootstrap should have ended.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Server-process arbitrary code execution
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to execute attacker-selected commands or code with a server process's privileges.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Duplicate asynchronous operation reissue
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to issue the same retry work twice, disrupting progress and ownership lifecycle.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Access through a released object reference
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to read, write, or invoke through an object reference after the object's lifetime has ended.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Protected transport-prefix substitution
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability for an active intermediary to delete or replace initial protected protocol messages without detection.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Rogue authenticated-session state transition
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to substitute authentication/session messages so the endpoint adopts an attacker-selected identity transition.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Stale parent-child lifecycle propagation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to suppress a parent cleanup transition because child state is propagated before its final update.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.concept: Dangling dispatch path retained after child deletion
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::c.description: Ability to retain and later invoke a dispatch or scheduling path through a freed child object.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Security-relevant state invariant enforcement
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Fixes which preserve valid lifecycle transitions and reject incompatible state.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Dispatch only the validated reassembled message
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Discard constituents after reconstruction so only one validated message is dispatched.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Guarded decommission with custody reconciliation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Prevent feature disablement while assets remain routed to the feature, or migrate custody before disablement.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Propagate fallible-operation errors before dependent work
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Return normal operation errors and clean state before assertions or downstream arithmetic.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Canonical security-decision representation enforcement
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Use one specified representation for security-sensitive comparisons.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Cancel and drain asynchronous work before teardown
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Ensure outstanding callbacks complete or are cancelled before dependent state is freed.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Validate URL authority grammar before reconstruction
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Reject malformed authority data or fall back to trusted server metadata so parsed paths remain scope-consistent.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Relocate rejection to context-specific operation boundaries
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Keep shared dependency reads available while applying invalid-state checks only where required.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Reservation-aware lock acquisition with failure handling
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Use a lock primitive and control flow that detects same-path reservation conflicts without deadlock.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Reuse valid recent state instead of repeating cooldown-protected work
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Skip a redundant mandatory operation when a sufficiently recent result already exists.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Reject semantically incompatible configuration at admission
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Enforce mode and direction constraints before configuration reaches runtime processing.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Suppress fallback-anchor updates after integrity rejection
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Retain the prior verified fallback when a candidate trips divergence or integrity checks.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Framing-preserving HTTP forwarding
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Use standards-compliant serialization that prevents field values from defining message boundaries.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Bind asynchronous browser actions to document identity
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Dismiss an action if its creation-time document or inner-window identity is no longer current.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Authorize before billable or irreversible processing
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Move authorization to the earliest phase before external charges or other irreversible effects.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Reentrancy-tolerant queued state-machine processing
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Serialize reentrant requests through a queue and resume logic rather than relying on captured state.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Enforce operation preconditions for object lifecycle state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Exclude object states lacking the initialization required by an operation.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Terminate shutdown wait when a fatal error preempts completion
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Ensure a fatal connection error ends or otherwise resolves a pending clean-shutdown wait.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Enforce domain blocking before hostile page execution
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Block navigation at a browser or network request boundary outside page-controlled DOM execution.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Restrict protocol-specific provisioners to their authorization flow
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Reject generic token-bearing requests that attempt to select a protocol-specific authorization implementation.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Revoke pending authority transitions during emergency recovery
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Clear queued authority changes so compromised control cannot survive recovery.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Invalidate bootstrap authorization after initial setup
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Expire and remove one-time setup credentials when bootstrap completes.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Single coherent retry lifecycle with progress accounting
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Leave reissue to one retry loop while consistently accounting progress and ownership flags.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Strict key-exchange transcript and sequence enforcement
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Bind key activation and initial protected messages so prefix deletion or substitution is detected.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.concept: Update child state before parent lifecycle propagation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::m.description: Make the final child state visible before parent notification and cleanup decisions.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::i.description: Unauthorized disclosure of protected information or secrets.
Disclosure of a flag, token, cookie-protected value, or comparable secret.
Loss of service, process, kernel, or protocol operation availability.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::i.concept: Kernel panic or fatal kernel fault
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::i.description: Kernel termination or fatal fault causing system availability loss.
Inability to complete required protocol, settlement, upgrade, or governance operations.
Access to a protected route, resource, or operation without required authorization.
Out-of-bounds or use-after-free access violating memory integrity.
Read, write, or dispatch through freed storage.
Read beyond the valid bounds of an object or stack region.
Unauthorized corruption or manipulation of security-relevant data, state, or outcomes.
Unauthorized token loss, stranded value, or financially material incorrect pricing.
Attacker-controlled JavaScript execution under another origin's authority.
Issuance of a CA certificate without the required authorization protocol.
Failure to durably remove or isolate compromised privileged authority.
Arbitrary command or code execution with server process privileges.
A session adopts an attacker-selected identity or authentication transition.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-01::i.concept: Continued exposure to blocked phishing content

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::s.concept: Local control of a kernel subsystem interface

A local process can arrange kernel object, socket, process, or filesystem lifecycle operations through exposed APIs.
Device attachment, removal, or physical interaction can drive a security-relevant lifecycle transition.
A remote party controls structured values consumed by a service or protocol endpoint.
An attacker controls a destination value later used for user navigation.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::s.concept: Managed-runtime finalizer interaction with native calls
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::s.description: A managed object with native-owned storage can be finalized while native code is in flight.
A remote peer controls protocol messages and state transitions.
A physically present actor can issue security-sensitive UI actions during device state transitions.
A contract user can invoke a flow containing an attacker-influenced callback and nested contract execution.
A guest controls state consumed by host-side virtualization or device management logic.
A remote unauthenticated requester controls HTTP framing and content.
A web origin can orchestrate popups, focus transitions, and elicited user clicks.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: An operation can reach, finalize, or destroy an object outside its valid ownership or liveness interval.
A transaction leaves an object updateable or reachable after deletion has made destruction pending.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Finalization after releasing the last protected reference
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: Object finalization proceeds after reference release without retaining required liveness and lock conditions.
Teardown can destroy callback-associated state while deferred work remains able to use it.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Native pointer use after managed finalization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: A finalizer can free wrapper-owned native storage before an in-flight native call stops using its pointer.
Two lifecycle paths independently destroy the same object.
A kernel memory-safety failure is usable for attacker-directed reads, writes, reuse, or repeated frees.
A security decision admits values outside the semantic type or value domain required by its invariant.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Non-integer values accepted by an integer predicate
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: A verifier evaluates language-level operations without first requiring intended integer operands.
A value authorized under one interpreter is consumed with materially different semantics by another.
Server-side origin approval is applied to an ambiguous URL that a browser resolves to another origin.
Peer-controlled transitions corrupt or bypass state retained for protocol safety.
A peer can remove a nonce or token that must remain retained for later protocol detection.
A lock-drop or concurrent transition invalidates assumptions required by rollback or restoration code.
Different consumers interpret one admitted encoded control value as conflicting ownership or disposition decisions.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Concurrent erasure of a shared exclusion guard
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: Cleanup outside the guard's synchronization boundary can erase state established by a later protected operation.
A security-sensitive action is accepted before its governing policy value has been loaded and applied.
A callback can enter a protected operation while its non-reentrant accounting interval is active.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Nested reuse of a balance-delta accounting interval
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: Nested operations reuse an initial balance snapshot and credit the same transferred value more than once.
A response or cached result is accepted without binding it to the semantic identity of its originating request.
A DNS response is cached for a name other than the queried name.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Auxiliary reference inconsistent with primary container state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: An auxiliary pointer or readiness indicator remains populated after the referenced item leaves its owning queue or container.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Dequeued OOB buffer retained as socket state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: A UNIX socket retains an OOB buffer reference after the buffer is removed from its receive queue.
Untrusted state is treated as authoritative inventory or identity for privileged lifecycle management.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Guest-controlled omission from host teardown inventory
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: Guest-mutable metadata can hide a provisioned device from host resource teardown.
Protocol output uses cryptographic state from an epoch that is not valid for the current handshake transition.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: TLS alert emitted with stale early-data protection
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: An alert after early data and HelloRetryRequest uses stale early-data write state before handshake traffic secrets are active.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.concept: Privileged batch continuation after context transition
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::c.description: A batched privileged dispatcher continues after an entry changes the caller's privilege or execution context.
Incorrect privilege or accounting state grants writable control over page tables.
A decision validates one state snapshot or object but execution consumes a different state.
Host nested-virtualization execution consumes guest controls that are not the same controls previously validated.
Inconsistent framing across intermediaries allows one client message to create an additional backend request.
HTTP framing ambiguity carries an attacker-built AJP request across the proxy boundary.
A smuggled backend request desynchronizes responses so attacker-selected output is delivered to another request.
Focus, activation, or modal-state divergence allows a sensitive control to accept an elicited click without its expected delay protection.
A browser permission control accepts a click after its focus or security-delay invariant has been bypassed.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Enforce object liveness and ownership before access or destruction
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Restore lifecycle ordering, exclusivity, reference retention, or transaction activity state before object use.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Deactivate transaction-deleted objects before later updates
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Mark a deleted object inactive in the next transaction generation before destruction can race with updates.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Finalize only while the last reference and required lock are retained
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Detect the last reference and run finalization under its required lock before releasing liveness.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Wait for deferred callback completion before teardown
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Synchronize teardown with outstanding callback completion.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Retain managed owners through native pointer use
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Keep each owning managed wrapper live until native calls using its storage have returned.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Exclude transaction-new objects from garbage collection
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Prevent GC from selecting not-yet-active objects whose destruction remains owned by transaction rollback.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Enforce the intended semantic operand domain before evaluation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Reject values outside the exact type and value domain before applying the security predicate.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Authorize and consume one canonical representation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Normalize an ambiguous value and use only the normalized representation after authorization.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Retain protocol detection state for its full validity window
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Do not let peer-controlled rejection paths evict state required for later detection.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Revalidate rollback preconditions after reacquiring synchronization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Check state openness and capacity before restoring data after a lock-drop interval.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Accept only semantically exact control encodings
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Reject parameterized encodings whose fields create conflicting downstream interpretations.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Keep shared guard cleanup inside its synchronization boundary
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Clear exclusion state only while the mutex governing the state remains held.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Gate security-sensitive actions on completed policy initialization
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Block authorization-sensitive actions until the governing policy has been read and applied.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Preserve reentrancy-guard history across storage-mode transitions
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Use sentinel state that remains meaningful across guard backing-mode activation and clearing.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Bind accepted responses to the originating request identity
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Require semantic request-response identity correspondence before caching or delivery.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Clear auxiliary references when removing primary state
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Atomically clear auxiliary pointers or readiness state when the referenced item leaves its primary container.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Use management-owned state as lifecycle authority
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Enumerate resources and resolve backend identity only from trusted management records.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Select protocol protection from the active epoch
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Emit and accept protocol records according to the protection state valid for the current handshake transition.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Terminate privileged batch dispatch after a context transition
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Represent a privilege-changing entry as batch exit or preemption and stop subsequent privileged operations.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Validate the exact state object consumed by execution
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Load state into its host-side execution object before validation and use that same validated object.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Upgrade to vendor-designated fixed implementation
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Deploy the vendor-fixed release when artifacts do not expose the source-level correction.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.concept: Gate sensitive UI acceptance on valid focus history
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::m.description: Reject sensitive control activation unless prior focus and anti-clickjacking state satisfy the acceptance invariant.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::i.concept: Process termination by stack exhaustion or fatal error
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::i.description: A remotely influenced error path terminates a client or service process.

A local actor gains kernel or root privilege.

A verifier bypass reaches output intended only after successful proof or challenge completion.
A trusted application causes users to navigate to an attacker-selected external origin.
A protocol safety detector fails to identify the condition it is designed to reject.
A protected execution window proceeds with its exclusion guard incorrectly cleared.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::i.concept: Financial or token accounting integrity loss
protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::i.description: Asset credit or balance accounting exceeds the value actually transferred.
A resolver serves attacker-selected cached resolution data.

protocol_and_lifecycle_state::part-02::i.concept: Host resource exhaustion or management obstruction

A user is induced to authorize a browser or application permission without a valid protected decision flow.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Attacker-influenced structured data supplied to a parser, decoder, matcher, or protocol implementation.
Attacker-controlled HTTP request body, header, or encoded header field section.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Untrusted protocol message or control sequence
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Attacker-controlled packet, frame sequence, length prefix, or protocol state transition.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Untrusted document, archive, or compiler artifact
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Attacker-controlled file or serialized document processed by a parser, codec, compiler, or archive reader.
Caller-controlled string, object graph, expression environment, pattern, or other in-process API value.
Input requiring an authenticated, administrative, or otherwise privileged actor to select processing behavior or content.
Connectionless input carrying a forged source address toward which a server sends responses.
Incorrect-credential attempts directed at a selected account by an unauthenticated party.
Growth of protocol or application state that raises the cost of a later bounded execution operation.
Attacker input causes work, memory, storage, stack, concurrency, or network output to exceed an intended resource relationship or bound.
Cyclic or deeply nested structures cause recursion without effective depth or cycle termination.
Malformed input drives repeated processing without forward state progress or a terminating error return.
A backtracking regex engine explores an excessive unsuccessful match space on crafted input.
Input cardinality causes quadratic or combinatorial synchronous search or comparison work.
Parser work is controlled by nesting, token count, field count, or structural complexity not bounded by serialized bytes alone.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Untrusted size or count driven heap allocation
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: An attacker-controlled size, count, or derived cardinality directly drives excessive heap allocation or retention.
Compact compressed, aliased, or encoded input expands into disproportionately large materialized output.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Unbounded input ingestion and downstream processing
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Input bytes are read, retained, persisted, extracted, encoded, or parsed without an ingress or aggregate-size budget.
Attacker-influenced cardinality determines a dynamic stack allocation large enough to crash the process.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Unbounded protocol buffering or object retention
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Protocol or ownership state retains queued packets or host objects without a finite release or backpressure bound.
Work continues after protocol accounting releases capacity, allowing active work to exceed the configured concurrency bound.
A client-controlled refresh path repeatedly forces expensive uncached backend work.
Attacker-controlled content reaches expensive browser rendering or highlighting despite oversized-content metadata.
A spoofable unvalidated UDP address induces server response bytes or retransmissions toward a third party.
Unauthenticated failed attempts consume and renew the lockout budget of a selected victim account.
State-dependent iteration makes a required blockchain synchronization call exceed the block gas limit and revert.
Enforce a finite budget before or during attacker-influenced processing.
Track depth or active traversal state and terminate excessive or cyclic recursion with an error.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Enforce forward progress and terminating error paths
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Reject non-forward boundaries or return from failed operations instead of looping.
Rewrite matching or delimiter recognition so crafted input cannot trigger catastrophic regex backtracking.
Use hashing, candidate restriction, or an explicit search budget to avoid superlinear exploration.
Bound nesting, tokens, items, fields, declarations, or decoded field-list size before expensive materialization.
Apply an element-, message-, or protocol-appropriate cap before heap allocation or retention.
Limit decompressed, alias-expanded, or otherwise materialized output before excessive allocation.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Bound input ingestion and aggregate metadata
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Apply byte or aggregate metadata limits before full reads, persistence, extraction, or token accumulation.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Move attacker-sized temporary storage off the stack
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Replace request-sized stack allocation with heap-backed storage and controlled allocation-error handling.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Bound retained buffers with backpressure or release
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Cap queued or owned objects and block, release, or error when the cap is reached.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Bound active work and deferred queues
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Count still-running work against concurrency limits and bound any deferred request queue.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Reuse cached data or bound response work
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Prevent repeated full refresh work through caching or a bounded response subset.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Gate expensive client rendering by size metadata
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Honor oversized-content metadata before highlighting or normal rendering and use a safe fallback.
Use a fixed release when supplied artifacts do not disclose the exact restored implementation invariant.
Rate-limit unvalidated sources or reduce retransmissions before address validation.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Scope incorrect-password throttling to the request source
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Prevent unauthenticated incorrect-password traffic from consuming a selected account's lockout budget.

resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.concept: Keep synchronization work within block gas
resource_exhaustion_and_complexity::part.description: Bound state cardinality or reduce iteration so required synchronization remains executable.
Loss or degradation of timely access to a process, service, client, account, or protocol operation.

Excessive computation, looping, or parsing delays or denies timely processing.
A victim browser page becomes unresponsive due to attacker-controlled client-side work.
A selected legitimate account is prevented from authenticating.
A server is abused to direct amplified traffic toward a spoofed third party.
A required synchronization transaction cannot execute within platform resource limits.
Parsing reaches a documented excessive-allocation failure condition without evidence sufficient to claim full service denial.

An actor can cause a backend to communicate with a remote peer under attacker control.

Attacker-derived keys or prototype state cross the boundary between inert application data and inherited JavaScript behavior.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.concept: Prototype influence over privileged internal lists

Accepted field data introduces a delimiter recognized later as a separate logical record.
Attacker-controlled records or state become authoritative authentication material.

A decoder delivers a value outside the type domain promised to downstream consumers.

Untrusted data reaches a .NET object deserializer with a command-capable gadget graph.
Untrusted Java serialization or RMI data reaches object restoration with usable gadget behavior.
Untrusted bytes reach pickle or pickle-enabled NumPy loading.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.concept: Python object construction during YAML loading
serialization_and_object_integrity::part.description: Untrusted YAML selects Python object or callable constructors during parsing.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.concept: PHP object deserialization with lifecycle behavior
serialization_and_object_integrity::part.description: Untrusted PHP serialized data instantiates objects and activates autoload or lifecycle gadget behavior.
Untrusted Hessian input can select object types without an explicit class authorization boundary.
Object restoration invokes a callback that enters attacker-configured executable application behavior.
A serialized expression or predicate crosses IPC and is evaluated with receiver-process authority.

A token or session minted before authentication is reusable at a privileged downstream endpoint.

Encoded path syntax is interpreted differently across routing and application boundaries, selecting an unintended route.
Client-supplied fields are consumed as if generated by a trusted proxy or upstream service.
Attacker-selected resources produce distinguishable responses revealing whether they exist.
Disclosed signing state and a collision or key-recovery weakness permit attacker-selected content to pass signature acceptance.
A mutable snapshot restores attacker-controlled executable runtime state without integrity verification.
A security filter and downstream parser decode key spellings differently, preserving a protected parameter.
Input selects and constructs an executable language callable which is later invoked.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.description: Do not restore executable object graphs from untrusted input; use a constrained schema and data-only format.

Remove restoration callbacks that enter application execution behavior.

Consume metadata only from a cryptographically authenticated upstream-service payload.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.concept: Serialized object-graph confinement at IPC boundary
serialization_and_object_integrity::part.description: Restrict accepted IPC object graphs to data-only receiver-authorized behavior.

serialization_and_object_integrity::part.description: Revert or discard results when a sub-operation fails instead of storing failure data as valid state.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker-controlled cross-site web origin
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A third-party page initiates a credentialed request or frames and manipulates a privileged interface.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Untrusted distributed-system peer metadata
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A peer across a cluster trust boundary supplies metadata later rendered to an operator.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker control across a browser content-interpretation boundary
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Untrusted data changes browser parsing from inert data into markup, style, template syntax, navigation code, or generated JavaScript.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: HTML markup injection
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Untrusted data is interpreted as HTML elements or attributes rather than inert text.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: HTML attribute-boundary injection
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-controlled data terminates or changes an HTML attribute or attribute-name parsing context.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: CSS injection into a privileged browser UI
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Untrusted rendered markup introduces attacker-chosen CSS without establishing arbitrary JavaScript execution.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Client template-expression execution
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Untrusted display data is evaluated by a client-side template expression interpreter.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Executable JavaScript-URI navigation
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: An attacker-controlled javascript scheme is persisted or admitted as a browser navigation target.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Generated-JavaScript string-context breakout
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Untrusted data escapes a quoted argument or string in generated JavaScript source.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Cross-decoder JavaScript syntax injection
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Different server and browser character representations turn accepted data into executable punctuation after decoding.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser-effective HTML reconstructed after parser-differential validation
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Parser and serializer disagreement allows executable markup absent from validated intermediate trees.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker-controlled browser JavaScript execution
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker code executes in a victim, operator, administrator, extension, or bot browser origin.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser script execution through injected markup event handling
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Injected markup executes JavaScript through an event handler such as onload or onerror.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser execution through an injected script element
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A reconstructed or admitted script element executes in the affected origin.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Injected script execution authorized by a synthesized CSP token
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker markup executes because its script authorization token matches the response policy.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Script execution with an unauthorized sandbox origin privilege
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker script executes on a selected sandbox suborigin after an improper same-origin grant.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser JavaScript execution through a client template expression
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A client template expression reaches JavaScript execution in the page context.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser script execution by following a JavaScript URI
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Victim navigation to an admitted javascript URI executes attacker code in the browser context.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser script execution from cross-decoder syntax injection
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Decoder-produced JavaScript punctuation yields executable script in the browser.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker control of a dynamic script-loader URL
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-controlled state supplies the URL used by a dynamically created script element.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Script access to origin-bound secret data
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Executing browser script can read a cookie, local-storage value, blob, frame document, or comparable origin-bound secret.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker-observable browser data signaling
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Browser behavior encodes victim data into attacker-observable requests or submissions.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: CSS-conditioned character request signaling
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Injected CSS conditionally issues requests based on displayed character matches.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: External form submission from untrusted proxy-origin content
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Proxy-served active content can submit victim-entered form data to an attacker-selected endpoint.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Bypass of browser security-policy authority
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker input obtains authority that a browser isolation, authorization, or content policy was intended to withhold.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker synthesis of a CSP-authorized nonce
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A nonce derived from attacker-controlled markup can be solved so injected script is authorized by CSP.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Unauthorized same-origin sandbox privilege
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: State-dependent token authorization adds allow-same-origin to untrusted sandboxed content.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker-induced renderer-origin collision
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Leaked and predictable per-render values let attacker content share an origin intended for a privileged renderer.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker control of protected template composition
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Coercion and framing ambiguities let untrusted data select or omit protected template pieces.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Cross-site authenticated state-changing request
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A third-party origin can cause a cookie-authenticated state change without intent-bound proof.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Unauthorized privileged-account creation
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A forged authenticated operation creates an administrator account.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: UI-redress control of a privileged embedded interface
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: An arbitrary origin frames a sensitive interface and induces interactions with disguised privileged controls.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Privileged credential population into attacker-controlled fields
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A credential manager or extension fills a selected victim credential into fields controlled by the attacker.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: DOM named-property corruption of security-sensitive state
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Injected named elements replace or supply JavaScript-visible properties used by security-sensitive logic.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Sanitizer safe-path bypass through clobbered capability lookup
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-mutated DOM state causes a sanitizer to return unsanitized input through a fallback.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Server-side template execution from untrusted template content
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Request-controlled data crosses an unescaped or later-evaluated server template boundary.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Server-process code execution
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: The attacker executes code in the affected server platform context.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Attacker-selected cryptographic operation context
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Ambient receiver state substitutes attacker-chosen algorithm or key context for a cryptographic operation.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Executable data response disables sanitizer security state
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Executable callback syntax mutates sanitizer support state so later sanitization becomes ineffective.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Rebinding of a nonce-authorized relative script loader
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-controlled document base state redirects a nonce-bearing relative script load to an attacker origin.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Cross-window opener URL read
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A retained opener and navigation relationship exposes a privileged URL containing secret material.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Preserve inert interpretation of untrusted browser content
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Restores the intended browser text, attribute, markup, or generated-code context for untrusted values.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Context-appropriate HTML text and attribute encoding
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Encodes dynamic values for their precise HTML text or attribute context.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Render untrusted content as text or policy-sanitized HTML
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Uses inert text rendering or an allowlist sanitizer so untrusted content cannot become active markup.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Context-preserving serialization of generated JavaScript strings
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Applies JavaScript string escaping when values are embedded in generated source.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: HTML-context auto-escaping template engine
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Uses a template engine that automatically escapes interpolated values for HTML output.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Validate or sanitize the final browser-effective document under one policy
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Eliminates parser and serializer disagreement by checking the representation delivered to the browser.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Keep untrusted values outside executable template contexts
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Prevents request or display data from entering server or client template evaluation contexts.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Structured URI parsing with an HTTP(S) scheme allowlist
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Only canonical parsed destinations with permitted non-executable schemes are accepted.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Fixed canonical response encoding shared by validator and browser
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Uses a server-controlled browser-supported encoding so validated characters cannot decode into different syntax.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Independent unpredictable browser-policy authorization tokens
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Generates authorization material independently of attacker input and without predictable reuse.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Stateless canonical sandbox-token authorization
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Evaluates every sandbox token independently and rejects forbidden privileges before mutation.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: CSP prohibition of form submission from untrusted content
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Restores the proxy-origin form-submission boundary with form-action none.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Use immutable application-owned DOM capabilities and configuration
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Security decisions and loader configuration do not resolve through attacker-clobberable named DOM properties.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Intent-bound validation for authenticated state changes
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Requires a session-bound CSRF token or equivalent proof before processing a state change.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Prevent untrusted origins from framing privileged UI
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Removes sensitive externally frameable resources or restricts frame ancestors.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Unguessable per-instance renderer secret with navigation-bound delivery
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Binds one unpredictable renderer secret to one intended navigation and prevents reuse or leakage.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Strict semantic validation with parser-owned message framing
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Uses whole-value validation and a real framing parser rather than coercion or raw delimiter splitting.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Explicit immutable cryptographic operation context
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Passes or binds cryptographic parameters explicitly instead of deriving them from ambient receiver state.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Confidentiality disclosure
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Unauthorized disclosure of protected information.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Credential or session-secret disclosure
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Passwords, credential values, or session cookies become available to an attacker.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Application secret or challenge-flag disclosure
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: A protected application secret, local-storage value, blob, flag, or decryption key is disclosed.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Browser-context code execution
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-controlled JavaScript executes in a victim-facing web or extension origin.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Cross-site scripting in an application browser context
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker-controlled browser script executes through application-rendered or serialized content.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Application or account integrity loss
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: The attacker causes unauthorized actions, state changes, UI compromise, or control of application behavior.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Server platform and connected-system compromise
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Server-context code execution compromises tenant data or connected internal systems.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Privilege escalation or privileged-account takeover
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: The attacker obtains or creates administrative authority.

web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.concept: Unauthorized action in a victim session
web_output_and_browser_execution::part-0.description: Attacker code or a forged request causes application actions under a victim's authenticated authority.
